_schema_note: Mirrors the LE10/LE11 convergence_study schema, BUT this case is NOT a tier_2_validated agreement. It is a documented SOLVER-LIMIT study: ccx (solid-shell) converges to ux@A = 0.2004 m, +8.3% above the NAFEMS thin-shell reference 0.185 m. The per-rung `within_case_tolerance` flags are computed against an HONEST 3% agreement band (the same band LE10/LE11 meet) and are FALSE for the converged rungs — recorded deliberately, not hidden.
refinement_units: S8R quad shell elements per meridian / sweep edge (expands to C3D20R solid)
_trend_monotone_note: ux@A increases monotonically with refinement toward a CONVERGED ccx value of ~0.2004 m. The residual vs the 0.185 thin-shell reference therefore GROWS with refinement (+5.74% -> +8.31%) and stabilises at +8.3% — refinement does NOT close the gap because the gap is a formulation difference, not a discretisation error.
notes: NAFEMS LE3 hemispherical shell, x-displacement at the loaded equator point A=(10,0,0). Real ccx 2.23, quadratic S8R shell (-> solid C3D20R), quarter model (pi/2 about z), translational-only symmetry, 2 kN outward at A + 2 kN inward at C, uz=0 at apex E. ccx converges UP to 0.2004 m. ROOT CAUSE: ccx has no true thin-shell element; a point load on the expanded solid shell adds a local 3-D dimple absent from thin-shell theory. CROSS-CHECK: Altair OptiStruct CQUAD4 (true thin shell) converges DOWN to the reference (normalized 0.9865/1.0200/1.0076/1.0032/1.0016 at 4/8/16/32/64 per edge => ~0.1853 @64). The two element families bracket the answer; the +8.3% is the documented thin-shell-vs-solid-shell divergence under a concentrated load. This case is recorded as an honest solver-capability boundary, NOT a benchmark agreement, and is deliberately excluded from the validated cohort.

optistruct_thin_shell_crosscheck.source: Altair OptiStruct OS-V:0030 (CQUAD4 first-order thin shell), normalized to 0.185 m
optistruct_thin_shell_crosscheck.interpretation: Thin-shell elements converge DOWN to 0.185; ccx solid-shell converges UP to 0.2004. Bracketing confirms the +8.3% is a formulation difference, not an error.
